distractor_misconceptions: a commit stores only the lines that changed, not a full snapshot of every tracked file
a commit's snapshot leaves out files that were not touched, instead of reusing their already-stored content
Git stores a computed diff as the commit, rather than a full snapshot compared later on demand
merging must always create a new commit, even when Git can finish with a fast-forward
staging a file that still contains conflict markers clears the unmerged status and finishes the merge properly
`git merge --abort` is confused with completing a conflicted merge, rather than cancelling it
